issue_title: Add strings to the mini-language: literals, concat, len, upper
issue_body:
Building on the integer mini-language exposed as tbx.Run, add a string data type. Strings must thread through the whole language alongside integers; every existing numeric behaviour from the first stage must keep working unchanged.

New capabilities:
  - String literals written with double quotes: "hello". Two escape sequences are supported inside a literal: \" for a double quote and \n for a newline.
  - The + operator becomes type-aware: integer + integer adds (as before); string + string concatenates; mixing an integer and a string is a type error. On a type error tbx.Run returns a single 'error: <msg>' line (exact message text is your choice; only the 'error: ' prefix matters).
  - print of a string outputs its raw character content (no surrounding quotes).
  - Two builtin functions, each taking one argument: len(x) returns the length of a string as an integer; upper(x) returns the string with its characters upper-cased.

The other operators (-, *, /) and unary minus remain integer-only. All of stage one's behaviour (let, print, integer arithmetic, precedence, parentheses, unary minus, truncating division, whitespace, undefined-variable and parse errors) must continue to hold exactly as before, and integers and strings must be able to coexist in the same program.

Keep the implementation a clean multi-file package and continue to expose everything through tbx.Run(src string) string.
prompt:
Extend the existing mini-language interpreter (exposed as tbx.Run(src string) string) by adding a string data type. Strings must integrate with the language alongside integers, and every numeric behaviour from the first stage must keep working exactly as before.

Add:
- String literals in double quotes: "hello". Inside a literal, support two escapes: \" for a double quote and \n for a newline.
- A type-aware + operator: integer + integer adds (as before); string + string concatenates; mixing an integer and a string is a type error. On a type error, tbx.Run returns a single 'error: <msg>' line (message text is your choice; only the 'error: ' prefix matters).
- print of a string outputs its raw character content, with no surrounding quotes.
- Two single-argument builtins: len(x) returns the length of a string as an integer, and upper(x) returns the string upper-cased.

The operators -, *, / and unary minus stay integer-only. Everything from the first stage (let, print, integer arithmetic with precedence and associativity, parentheses, unary minus, truncating integer division, whitespace handling, and the undefined-variable / parse-error reporting) must still behave identically, and integers and strings must coexist within one program. Keep the implementation a clean multi-file package and continue exposing it through tbx.Run.
expected_behavior: All stage-one numeric behaviour still works: let, print, integer + - * / with correct precedence and associativity, parentheses, unary minus, truncating division, whitespace, and 'error: <msg>' for undefined variables and parse failures.
String literals with \" and \n escapes parse and print their raw content.
string + string concatenates; integer + integer still adds; mixing an integer and a string yields a single 'error: <msg>' line.
len(s) returns the string length as an integer and upper(s) returns the upper-cased string.
Integers and strings can be used together in the same program.
skills_tested: threading a new value type through an existing lexer, parser, and evaluator
lexing quoted string literals with escape sequences
type-aware operator overloading and type-error reporting
registering builtin functions in the parser and evaluator
preserving carried-over behaviour while extending a language
